en: be refused; be rejected; be denied

examples.en: My visa application was rejected.
My proposal gets turned down again.
I was once refused entry at a store.
I could not speak up, fearing I would be rejected.
I keep getting rejected, so I feel upset.
It hurts when a friend rejects you.

explain: '당하다'가 붙어서 내가 받아 주기를 바랐는데 상대가 안 받아 주었다는 속상한 느낌이 있어요. 단순히 안 받아들여진 일은 '거부되다', 상대가 내게 한 일로 느낄 때는 '거부당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The '당하다' ending adds an unhappy feeling that someone refused you when you wanted it accepted. A plain event of not being accepted uses '거부되다', while '거부당하다' feels like something done to you.

examples.en: A firefighter rescued the child.
They rescue people who fell into the sea.

examples.ko: 산에서 길을 잃은 사람들을 구조할 거예요.
examples.en: They will rescue the people lost in the mountains.
The rescue took two hours.
I have rescued a stray dog before.

examples.ko: 다친 사람들을 무사히 구조해 줘서 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you for rescuing the injured people safely.

explain: 위험에 빠진 사람이나 동물을 도와서 벗어나게 할 때 써요. '도와주다'는 일상의 도움이고, '구조하다'는 사고나 재난처럼 위험한 상황에 써요. 구조받는 쪽은 '구조되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when you help a person or animal escape danger. '도와주다' covers everyday help, while 구조하다 is for accidents and disasters. The one rescued uses '구조되다'.

examples.ko: 사람이 많은 지하철에서는 소매치기를 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should watch out for pickpockets on a crowded subway.
A pickpocket took my wallet at the market.
I saw news that the police caught a pickpocket.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 소매치기 조심하라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Before the trip, I was told to beware of pickpockets.

examples.ko: 저는 어제 버스 정류장에서 소매치기를 당할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got pickpocketed at the bus stop yesterday.

examples.ko: 소매치기가 많은 곳에서는 가방을 앞으로 메요.
examples.en: In places with many pickpockets, I wear my bag in front.

explain: 피해를 입었을 때는 '소매치기를 당하다'라고 하고, 소매치기를 하는 사람도 소매치기라고 불러요. '도둑'은 훔치는 사람 전체를 부르고, 소매치기는 사람이 많은 곳에서 몰래 가져가는 도둑이에요.
explain_en: When you are the victim, you say 소매치기를 당하다, and the thief is also called 소매치기. 도둑 covers any thief, while 소매치기 is one who quietly takes things in crowded places.

en: be taken away; be arrested and taken away

examples.en: The thief was caught and taken away by the police.

examples.ko: 아이가 낯선 사람에게 잡혀가는 꿈을 꿨어요.
examples.en: I had a dream that a child was taken away by a stranger.
In old tales, the bad people get taken away.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 왜 잡혀갔는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows why that person was taken away.
If you do wrong, you could be taken to the police station.
After the criminal was taken away, the town became quiet.

explain: '잡다'에 피동을 만드는 '-히-'가 붙은 '잡히다'와 '가다'가 합쳐진 말이에요. 잡는 쪽이 주어면 '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', 잡힌 사람이 주어면 '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'라고 해요. 잡는 사람 뒤에는 '에게'나 '한테'를 붙여요.
explain_en: It combines '잡히다' (the passive of '잡다') with '가다'. If the catcher is the subject you say '경찰이 도둑을 잡아가요', and if the caught person is the subject you say '도둑이 경찰에게 잡혀가요'. The person who catches gets '에게' or '한테'.

en: come to invade; come to attack

examples.en: The enemy suddenly attacked the castle.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 우리 집에 쳐들어와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A stranger barged into our house and I was shocked.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님들이 가게로 쳐들어올까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried the angry customers might storm into the shop.

examples.ko: 친구들이 갑자기 쳐들어오는 바람에 청소를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My friends barged in suddenly, so I couldn't clean.

examples.ko: 게임에서 적이 우리 진영으로 쳐들어오고 있어요.
examples.en: In the game, the enemy is charging into our camp.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 이웃 나라가 쳐들어온 적이 있어요.
examples.en: A long time ago, a neighboring country invaded.

explain: 말하는 사람 쪽으로 힘차게 들어오는 것을 말해서 '쳐들어가다'와 방향이 반대예요. 전쟁뿐 아니라 갑자기 들이닥치는 사람에게도 써요. 딱딱한 말은 '침입하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes someone forcefully coming in toward the speaker, so its direction is the opposite of '쳐들어가다'. It is used for wars and also for people who suddenly burst in. The stiffer word is '침입하다'.
